Each spring, thousands of attendees from near and far make their way to New Orleans’ historic French Quarter for the annual French Quarter Festival (FQF). This massive celebration highlights the food, music, art, and culture of this beloved neighborhood. Spanning from the scenic Riverfront to the lively Jackson Square, the festival invites visitors to savor signature dishes crafted by local chefs, dance to performances by renowned artists, and explore interactive activities that bring the neighborhood’s charm to life. Beyond the main attractions, pop-up art installations, second-line parades, and cultural demonstrations add layers of excitement to this immersive celebration of all things New Orleans. You can learn more about most of the musicians performing at French Quarter Festival this year via our Artist database, powered by our partners at WWOZ-FM. You'll find bios, photos, playlists, and more. For the full lineup and more details on this year's festival, download the French Quarter Festival app (iOS) (Android) or visit their site at FrenchQuarterFest.org. 2026 French Quarter Fest Music Lineup The 2026 French Quarter Festival music lineup brings together New Orleans legends, fan favorites, and exciting new voices for more than 300 performances across the festival. This year’s highlights include Irma Thomas, Big Freedia, Kermit Ruffins & the Barbecue Swingers, Rebirth Brass Band, The Dirty Dozen Brass Band, George Porter Jr. & Runnin’ Pardners, Jon Cleary & the Absolute Monster Gentlemen, Shamarr Allen, Cyril Neville, Amanda Shaw, Lost Bayou Ramblers, and a highly anticipated debut from Dawn Richard. From brass bands and funk to zydeco, Cajun, soul, and global sounds, the festival celebrates the full spectrum of New Orleans music and culture. The full lineup and performance schedule will be released soon! 2026 French Quarter Fest Food Lineup Over 50 local restaurants and food vendors will serve classic New Orleans dishes and global flavors. Festival favorites include: Traditional New Orleans Fare: Jacques-Imos Cafe – Creole comfort classics Tujague’s Restaurant – Historic Creole cuisine Broussard’s – French-Creole staples Dickie Brennan’s Steakhouse – New Orleans beef and seafood favorites Desire Oyster Bar – Oysters and Gulf seafood Original New Orleans Po-Boys – Classic po-boys Seafood & Louisiana Specialties: Goodfellas Seafood & Po-Boys – Fried seafood and po-boys Voleo’s Seafood – Fresh Gulf seafood Redfish Grill – Cajun and Creole seafood International & Fusion Flavors: SunChong NOLA – Korean-inspired street food 9 Roses – Vietnamese favorites 14 Parishes – Jamaican jerk and Caribbean flavors LUFU NOLA – Indian-inspired tacos Sweet Treats & Festival Favorites: Loretta’s Authentic Pralines – Legendary pralines Plum Street Snoballs – Classic New Orleans snowballs Cafe Beignet – Fresh beignets Quintin’s Natural Ice Cream – Small-batch ice cream All food vendors accept credit cards and festival beverage tickets. Food booths are located throughout the festival grounds. French Quarter Fest History French Quarter Festival first debuted in 1984 as a way to celebrate and revitalize New Orleans’ historic French Quarter. Originally created to remind locals of the neighborhood's unique charm and encourage community pride, the festival quickly became a beloved tradition. What started as a small, local event has grown into one of the largest free music festivals in the United States, attracting hundreds of thousands of visitors each year. The celebration of music, food, and culture is now a cherished experience for locals and visitors alike, capturing the spirit of the Crescent City like no other event. Best Hotels for the French Quarter Fest Omni Royal Orleans Stay in the heart of the French Quarter Fest at the Omni Royal Orleans, the official hotel of the event. With its rooftop pool, stunning city views, and the acclaimed Rib Room restaurant, this hotel combines convenience with sophistication, making it an ideal choice for festival-goers. Royal Sonesta New Orleans Experience the perfect mix of luxury and excitement at The Royal Sonesta, located on iconic Bourbon Street. With live jazz at The Jazz Playhouse, gourmet dining at Restaurant R’evolution, and a tranquil courtyard pool, it’s a lively yet relaxing retreat that captures the spirit of the festival. The Windsor Court Hotel For those seeking understated elegance, The Windsor Court offers a peaceful stay just outside the French Quarter. Spacious suites, a rooftop pool, and fine dining at The Grill Room make it a haven for guests wanting to balance festival fun with relaxation. Things to Do Around French Quarter Fest If you’re visiting New Orleans for the French Quarter Festival, the neighborhood offers countless ways to make the most of your trip. Start with a stroll through Jackson Square, where local artists display their work and street performers bring the area to life. Walk along the Riverfront to enjoy breathtaking views of the Mississippi River, then explore the French Market for everything from handmade crafts to local snacks like pralines and hot sauce. For a taste of history, take a mule-drawn carriage ride through the French Quarter or visit the Historic New Orleans Collection to learn about the city’s unique past. Feeling adventurous? Join a ghost tour to uncover the eerie legends of this historic neighborhood. Nearby landmarks like the St. Louis Cathedral offer even more glimpses into the area’s storied charm. Food and drink are always highlights in the French Quarter. Sip chicory coffee and savor a beignet at Café du Monde, or try a po’ boy or fresh seafood platter at a nearby eatery. Head to a rooftop bar like Hot Tin for sweeping views of the city, or relax in the lush courtyards of French Quarter restaurants. Whether you’re wandering the streets, uncovering the city’s charm, or indulging in local flavors, the French Quarter is packed with fun to keep the excitement going!
